- **F-P08 (Learnopoly Deaf linguist):** Single commenter extracted from a multi-comment review page. A second commenter on the same page made a different statement about billing practices (not competitive positioning), so it was excluded per scope.

64_source_type_ambiguities:
- **Quora (F-P07, F-X07):** Assigned "unknown." Quora is a Q&A platform, not a forum, blog, or review aggregator. No clean mapping in the allowed shard taxonomy. Closest: seller_forum (if interpreted broadly as "forum") but Quora users are typically learners, not sellers.

- **BitDegree (F-P06):** Assigned "review_aggregator." BitDegree generates automated comparison pages with proprietary scoring. It functions more as a review aggregator than a traditional article or blog.

- **Crehana blog (F-P02) and Coderhouse blog (F-P09):** Assigned "blog." Both are competitor corporate blogs. These are editorial content on competitor-owned domains, functioning as content marketing. "blog" is technically correct but does not capture the adversarial-source nuance; noted here.

- **Learnopoly comment (F-P08):** Assigned "article." The parent page is a review article; the finding comes from its comment section. "article" is the closest match for the page type, though the specific text comes from a user comment, not the article author.

- **SD-10 (YouTube):** Complete gap. No YouTube transcripts surfaced in search. Video comparisons of Domestika (especially in Spanish) are known to exist based on TikTok cross-references but remain unverified.

- **SD-09 (Quora):** Near-complete gap. Only one snippet-based provisional finding (F-P07). Full Quora answers could not be accessed.

- **Spanish self-positioning (SD-01):** The primary Spanish About page (/es/info/about) could not be fetched directly. Spanish self-positioning text was captured from the Spanish homepage (/es) instead (F-03, F-04), supplemented by a LinkedIn mirror (F-X06). Coverage is partial but functional.

- **Domestika pricing page in Spanish (/es/plus):** Not separately fetched. English Plus page (/en/plus) was used for F-07. Spanish pricing copy may differ; this is unverified.
